questions.q: What does a PostgreSQL logical backup actually capture, per this lesson?
options: The database objects and data as SQL statements or a portable archive of them
A byte-for-byte copy of the raw data directory on disk
Only the transaction log files
A snapshot of memory, not disk
questions.explain: pg_dump and pg_dumpall produce SQL (or an archive format that reconstructs SQL) — CREATE TABLE, INSERT, CREATE INDEX, and so on.

questions.q: What does pg_basebackup use to pull a physical backup from a running server?
options: The streaming replication protocol
A plain HTTP file transfer
SQL INSERT statements
SSH with no defined protocol
questions.explain: pg_basebackup uses the same streaming replication protocol replicas use to pull a consistent copy of the data directory.

questions.q: Why can a logical backup be restored into a different PostgreSQL version or operating system, while a physical backup cannot?
options: A logical backup is SQL that gets replayed, while a physical backup is raw files tied to a specific major version and architecture
Logical backups are always smaller in file size
Physical backups are encrypted by default
There is no real difference between them on this point
questions.explain: SQL statements are portable; the on-disk file format a physical backup copies must match the target server's version and architecture exactly.

questions.q: Which scenario is the best fit for a logical backup, per this lesson?
options: Restoring a single truncated lookup table without touching the rest of the database
Recovering a 2 TB production database as fast as possible after a disk failure
Building a streaming replica
Establishing the base for point-in-time recovery
questions.explain: Logical backups support selective, partial restores — like one table — which physical backups don't do without extra tooling.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what do production PostgreSQL environments commonly do regarding backup strategy?
options: Run both logical dumps for flexibility and physical base backups plus WAL archiving for disaster recovery
Use only pg_dump and never touch physical backups
Avoid backups entirely and rely on replication alone
Use only filesystem snapshots with no logical backups at all
questions.explain: The two approaches solve different problems, so production environments typically combine them rather than picking just one.
